content.intro: This lesson covers Concurrency Versus Parallelism. It sits in Module 16, Concurrency and Parallel Programming, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Concurrency Versus Parallelism matters when you work with safe coordination across concurrent tasks. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Concurrency coordinates multiple tasks that may overlap in time. Rust uses ownership, Send/Sync bounds, message passing, and synchronization types to make shared access explicit.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Concurrency Versus Parallelism, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Concurrency can be achieved with threads, channels, and shared synchronization. Test failure paths and avoid holding locks longer than necessary.
